Punta Gorda (Belize)

Also find this entry through: Punta Gorda

Garifuna community life is part of Punta Gorda’s wider local society. This starting route focuses on public cultural organizing, children’s learning and a dated regional event report; older local histories and the town’s many communities need further attention.

01

A locally based cultural initiative

The Battle of the Drums Secretariat’s public programme text describes its beginning in Punta Gorda in 2006 and later formal organization. It presents music, language education and community support as connected parts of its work. This is the organization’s account, not an independent registration check or a claim that it speaks for all residents.

Read the sources [1] Battle of the Drums Secretariat

02

Learning beyond a single performance

The organization’s substantive FAQ describes classroom teaching, after-school activity and school contests, naming St. Peter Claver in Punta Gorda among a wider school network. These are described programme activities and aims. They do not by themselves show how many children participated or measure current learning outcomes.

Read the sources [1] Battle of the Drums Secretariat

03

A public stage with regional connections

PGTV’s December 2024 report places a competition at Punta Gorda Sporting Complex and describes participating groups from Belize, Guatemala and Honduras. It is a dated example of cross-border public culture. The performers are particular groups, not automatic representatives of every community or a complete account of Garifuna music.

Read the sources [2] PGTV Belize

Battle of the Drums — programme history and substantive FAQ ↗

The organization’s detailed programme and FAQ text describes beginning in Punta Gorda in 2006, later organization and cultural education work, including a named local school. Read these as its own account of aims and activities.

Inspection: Content reviewed for the stated scope

Scope: Actual indexed primary-site programme introduction and complete FAQ subsection read through ordinary search tool: origins/formalization, three programme pillars, PuntaGorda secretariat and named school rollout. Substantive programme text, not a bare homepage/index.

Review recorded: October 29, 2026

Access note: The related exact 2024-launch and 2025-classroom paths returned directHTTP403 and reader errors; stopped, no bypass. No full live homepage fetch, registry/tax verification, current totals, programme evaluation or completed teaching outcomes claimed. Financial/tax/donation advice, schedules and media excluded.
